profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This CyrusOne campus sits in Loudoun County, Virginia, in and around Sterling, part of the Northern Virginia Ashburn area data center corridor. Wikipedia coverage of CyrusOne states the company purchased 40 acres in Loudoun County in June 2016 for data center construction. CyrusOne was founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten, went public in 2013, and was taken private in 2022 when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts and Global Infrastructure Partners acquired it for 15 billion dollars. No building specific address or individual MW figures were located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Sterling campus publishes 116 MW of IT capacity, the largest single reported figure among Virginia facilities tracked here and roughly half of all reported Virginia megawatts.

The 116 MW represents power delivered to equipment across three buildings and 1.18 million square feet of technical space. At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, this would support approximately 2,900 racks; at typical enterprise density of 10 kW per rack, roughly 11,600 racks. CyrusOne publishes neither actual rack count nor target workload density, so these are calculation endpoints only, not operator claims.

Sterling sits within Northern Virginia, the densest data center region in the United States by most measures. This site holds no data on grid constraints, utility relationships, or power availability specific to this campus. The operator's spec page lists no certifications, so no inference about qualified workload types can be drawn from that source.

A reader assessing AI relevance should treat 116 MW as a floor on available capacity and seek operator or utility disclosures beyond these published facts for anything about power sourcing, grid stability, or workload restrictions.
